newsitem.title: CONGO: Boats with 34 refugees lost on Zaire river.
newsitem.headline: Boats with 34 refugees lost on Zaire river.

text.p: Two boats carrying 34 refugee Zaireans and Rwandan Hutus have disappeared on the Zaire river after a collision, a military source in Congo said on Friday.
The military source said the two boats disappeared on Wednesday night around 450 km (280 miles) north of the capital Brazzaville. He added that a search was underway for the missing refugees.
The 34 refugees were part of a mixed group of over 1,800 Zaireans and Rwandans, some of them armed, who had fled the advance of Laurent Kabila's rebels to the Congolese town of Liranga.
The arrival of the refugees sowed dissaray in Liranga as they raided local farms, stealing sugar cane and manioc to feed themselves.
Rwandan refugees fled to Zaire in 1994 to escape reprisals for the genocide of over 800,000 Tutsis and moderate Hutus.
When Kabila's Tutsi-dominated fighters launched their rebellion in October hundreds of thousands of Rwandan Hutus left camps along the eastern border and fled deeper into Zaire.
The U.N. refugee agency has repatriated over 13,000 refugees by plane from the rebel-occupied eastern Zaire city of Kisangani and expects to repatriate as many as 40,000 from there.
Other groups of refugees are scattered across Zaire and several thousands have trekked over 1,000 km (620 miles), as far as the border of Zaire's southeastern neighbour, Angola.
